papers.title: Liquation and Crystallization Cracks in Aluminum Alloy AA2024 during Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: In this work we studied the microstructure and microhardness of standard AA2024 alloy and AA2024 alloy with the addition of 1.5% Y after pulsed laser melting (PLM) and selective laser melting (SLM). The SLM process was carried out with a 300 W power and 0.1 m/s laser scanning speed. A dispersed microstructure without the formation of crystallization cracks and low liquation of alloying elements was obtained in Y-modified AA2024 aluminum alloy. Eutectic Al 3 Y and Al 8 Cu 4 Y phases were detected in Y-modified AA2024 aluminum alloy. It is led to a decrease in the formation of crystallization cracks The uniform distribution of alloying elements in the yttrium-modified alloy had a positive effect on the quality of the laser melting zone (LMZ) and microhardness.
papers.venue: Defect and diffusion forum/Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part A, Defect and diffusion forum

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究铝合金AA2024的SLM工艺和裂纹控制，与生物医学材料方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implant materials, porous structures for stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration; it focuses on aluminum alloy crack mitigation for non-biomedical applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究Y添加对AA2024铝合金SLM过程中裂纹的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用脉冲激光熔覆和选区激光熔化制备含Y的AA2024合金。
summary_zh.result: 添加Y后消除结晶裂纹，组织均匀，显微硬度提高。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微组织观察和显微硬度测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of yttrium addition on liquation and crystallization cracking in AA2024 aluminum alloy during selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Pulsed laser melting and selective laser melting were used to fabricate AA2024 alloy with 1.5% Y addition at 300 W and 0.1 m/s.
summary_en.result: Y-modified AA2024 exhibited a crack-free, dispersed microstructure with eutectic Al3Y and Al8Cu4Y phases, improving microhardness.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural analysis and microhardness testing confirmed the reduction of cracks and uniform element distribution.

papers.title: Computational Investigation of Tissue and Blood Vessel Growth Trade-Offs in Hierarchical Lattices
papers.abstract: Abstract Computational design is growing in necessity for advancing biomedical technologies, particularly when considering complex systems with numerous trade-offs among design decisions and resulting biomechanical behavior. In tissue engineering applications, porous bone scaffold structures enabled by 3D printing can have intricate lattice structures and hierarchical features that mimic the biological hierarchy of natural bone. However, these hierarchies create challenges in predicting the tissue regeneration process and how different scales of the hierarchy drive varied biological behaviors. Smaller pores facilitate tissue growth while larger pores are necessary for blood vessel growth, however, identifying favorable trade-offs to maximize growth of both tissue and blood vessels remains a challenge, especially for complex 3D printed structures. Here, we adapt tissue and blood vessel growth models for predicting biological growth in scaffolds with varied combinations of beam diameter size, unit cell topology, and hierarchical pore size/distribution. Findings demonstrate that on a normalized scale lattices with no large voids provide greater tissue growth but less blood vessel growth in comparison to lattice layouts with large void areas. A lattice with large void channels provided the greatest blood vessel growth but poorer tissue growth, while a lattice with evenly distributed large voids provided a better compromise between the two types of growth. Overall, these findings demonstrate the merit in computational investigations for design trade-off comparisons in tissue scaffolds, and provide a foundation for future explorations of biological design decisions for regenerative medicine and 3D printed systems.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索骨支架中不同层级孔隙对组织与血管生长的权衡
summary_zh.method: 采用组织与血管生长模型模拟不同梁直径、单元拓扑和层级孔隙的组合
summary_zh.result: 大空洞通道促进血管生长但抑制组织生长，均匀大空洞提供更好的折衷
summary_zh.validation: 纯计算模拟，未进行实验验证

summary_en.motivation: Investigate trade-offs between tissue and blood vessel growth in hierarchical bone scaffolds with varying pore sizes.
summary_en.method: Adapted tissue and blood vessel growth models to simulate biological growth in lattices with different beam diameters, unit cell topologies, and hierarchical pore distributions.
summary_en.result: Lattices with large void channels maximize blood vessel growth but reduce tissue growth, while evenly distributed large voids provide a better compromise.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely computational investigation.
